compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py::test_pinned_upstream_canary` fails on the
`optionality / terraform-config-inspect pinned canary` job with
`AssertionError: assert 'abstain' == 'match'`, on changes that are fully up to date with `main`.
Observed on Gerrit change 2674, whose base is `0033662b5534` (current `main`), in
`https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/33961826977/job/101295228786`. Rebasing does not
help. The job runs on every patchset, so this blocks the review queue.

`go install` is NOT the cause. Its step in that job logs ten successful module downloads and
reports no error, and the test's own `has_binary` guard passed — execution reached line 429/446,
well past it. The `"go install silently failed"` string in the log is the pytest source listing
rendered in the traceback context, not the assertion that fired.

## Root cause

The corroborator abstains `config_inspect_schema_skew`. Reproduced locally and deterministically
against the audited binary (`go install
github.com/hashicorp/terraform-config-inspect@2fb54c236733ee65ee877105d595c124c993c64d`, run from
a temp GOBIN):

```
outcome      : abstain
reason       : version_skew
reason_detail: config_inspect_schema_skew
```

`src/rebar/schemas/terraform_config_inspect.schema.json` is a producer contract that the pinned
tool's output can never satisfy. Validating one real invocation yields 15 violations in three
classes:

1. `pos` requires `column` and `byte`. Upstream `SourcePos` has exactly two fields —
   `Filename string` and `Line int` (`tfconfig/source_pos.go` at the pinned commit). Every
   positioned element therefore fails.
2. The top-level `required` list demands `required_core`, `provider_configs` and `diagnostics`.
   The tool omits all three when empty, so a clean module never carries them.
3. `resource.provider` is typed `["string", "null"]`. The tool emits an object, `{"name": "aws"}`.

Behind the schema sits a second, latent abstain. `tfconfig/load.go`'s `dirFiles` builds
`fullPath := filepath.Join(dir, name)` and hands that to the parser, so `pos.filename` echoes the
directory argument. `_run` passes the ABSOLUTE snapshot path
(`src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py:286`), so filenames come back absolute
(`/tmp/.rebar-tfci-xxxx/main.tf`), and `_validate_positions` rejects any absolute filename at
`src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py:367` with `path_outside_snapshot`. Fixing only the
schema would move the abstain, not remove it. Confirmed by running the tool both ways: with an
absolute dir argument `pos.filename` is `/tmp/realtf/snap/main.tf`; with `.` it is `main.tf`.

The unit suite never caught either because it does not use the real tool — `_fixture_binary`
builds a fake whose payload was written by hand, with `column`/`byte` fields the tool does not
emit and relative filenames it does not produce. The canary is the one test that touches reality.

This is a THIRD, independent defect alongside `persuasive-welcome-nymph` (a wall-clock race in the
fault test's own fixture) and `ergophilic-freudian-queenbee` (a CI step that fails on pre-gate
trees). Same provenance commit `59d504c2bdbb` / Gerrit 2672, three distinct mechanisms. In
particular the `JSONDecodeError` on `persuasive-welcome-nymph` is NOT this defect wearing a
different mask: that test points `PATH` at its own fake binary directory, so the audited tool is
irrelevant to it, and its exception comes from the test harness reading its own `capture.json`
(test file line 186), not from the corroborator parsing tool output.

## Approach

Correct the producer contract to the tool that is actually pinned, and stop feeding the tool a
path it will echo back:

1. In `terraform_config_inspect.schema.json`, make `pos` require only `filename` and `line`
   (keeping `column`/`byte` as optional properties so a tool revision that adds them still
   validates), drop `required_core`/`provider_configs`/`diagnostics` from the top-level `required`
   list while keeping them as optional properties, and type `resource.provider` as the
   `{name, alias}` object the tool emits, or null.
2. In `_run`, pass `"."` as the directory argument instead of the absolute snapshot path. The
   child's `cwd` is already the snapshot, so this is the same directory, and it makes the tool
   stamp relative `pos.filename`s that `_validate_positions` accepts without relaxing that check
   at all. It also strengthens the existing redaction posture, which already asserts that no argv
   element contains the repo path.
3. Update `test_subprocess_contract_strips_environment_and_copies_readonly_snapshot` to assert the
   new argv contract (`["--json", "."]` with `cwd` the snapshot) and keep its
   no-path-leak assertions, and update the recorded `invocation.argv` placeholder in
   `_match_result` to match.

Correcting the schema rather than loosening the abstain is the right shape here: the abstain
logic is sound (it refuses to emit T1 evidence it cannot ground), and the canary is correct to
refuse a vacuous pass. The defect is that the contract describes a tool that does not exist.

De-risked before codifying: with exactly these two changes applied in a throwaway harness against
the real audited binary, `variable.region` returns MATCH, `variable.missing` returns abstain
`no_unique_address`, and `module_source_equals` on `module.vpc` returns MATCH — the canary's own
assertions, satisfied.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/schemas/terraform_config_inspect.schema.json` — align `pos`, the top-level `required`
  list, and `resource.provider` with the pinned tool's real output.
- `src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py` — pass `"."` as the tool's directory argument in
  `_run`; update the recorded `invocation.argv` placeholder in `_match_result`.
- `tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py` — update the subprocess-contract
  assertions to the new argv, and the fake payload's `pos`/`provider` shape to the tool's real one
  so the fake stops contradicting the schema it is validated against.

## Testing

- RED, reproduced locally and deterministically: with the audited binary on `PATH`,
  `REBAR_TERRAFORM_CONFIG_INSPECT_CANARY=1 pytest -k pinned_upstream_canary` fails
  `assert 'abstain' == 'match'`, and a direct `corroborate_diagnostic` call reports
  `reason_detail=config_inspect_schema_skew`. Both recorded before the fix.
- GREEN, live end-to-end against the real boundary: the same canary command passes with the real
  audited binary installed, which is the only check that exercises the actual tool.
- Latent-path proof: after the schema fix alone, assert the corroboration still abstains
  `path_outside_snapshot`; after the `"."` change as well, it matches. This shows both links of
  the chain were necessary rather than assuming it.
- Regression: the whole `tests/unit/grounding/` tier passes with the fake fixture updated, and
  `pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py -q` reports the same
  pass/skip counts as before the change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the audited binary on `PATH`,
      `REBAR_TERRAFORM_CONFIG_INSPECT_CANARY=1 pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py -k pinned_upstream_canary`
      PASSES; recorded as a ticket comment alongside the pre-fix failure text.
- [ ] Validating one real `terraform-config-inspect --json .` document against
      `terraform_config_inspect.schema.json` yields zero violations; verified by a scripted
      `iter_errors` count of 0 (it is 15 today).
- [ ] `_run` passes `"."` as the directory argument and the child's `cwd` remains the snapshot;
      verified by the updated subprocess-contract test, which still asserts no argv element
      contains the repo path.
- [ ] Applying only the schema change leaves the corroboration abstaining
      `path_outside_snapshot`, demonstrating the second link was independently necessary;
      recorded as a ticket comment.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/grounding/ -q` is green and `make verify` is green before the change is
      pushed to Gerrit.

file_impact.reason: Align pos, the top-level required list, and resource.provider with the pinned tool's real output.
Pass '.' as the tool's directory argument so pos.filename stays relative; update the recorded invocation.argv placeholder.
Update the subprocess-contract argv assertions and the fake payload's pos/provider shape to the tool's real shape.
